2026-10-25: The day's strongest picks for a dexterity researcher are ARPG, which pretrains action representations on human hand data for compact generative dexterous policies, and AdaPolicy, which adds training-only next-chunk prediction to chunked policies. On the generative side, Cumulative Marginal Matching offers a principled marginal-level objective for one-step flow generation. A recurring theme is using auxiliary future prediction (video or action) only at training time to improve VLA and chunked policies at no inference cost.
2026-10-26: Top pick is Freeze, Don't Clone, which pins down an actor-side failure when fine-tuning flow and action-chunked policies online without offline data and fixes it by freezing the BC prior. FLORE shows a force-reactive diffusion policy for humanoid loco-manipulation trained from force-sensing UMI data, and DEX-PHD offers a portable dexterous-hand data collection device. World models as counterfactual engines (Rollback) and energy-based steering of frozen VLAs (JevVLA) round out a day centered on adapting pretrained policies.
2026-10-27: A strong day for dexterity: CARD retargets human demonstrations while preserving contact-force targets, and the LEAP-hand in-hand pose-reaching paper shows sim-only policies with learned safety filters transferring zero-shot. On the policy-architecture side, JAM untangles the VLA vs world-action-model debate and TAPESTRY treats actions as video patches in a pretrained video DiT. AFIL's use of failure rollouts as negative guidance for diffusion/flow VLAs and DexSuite's infrastructure are also worth a look.
2026-10-28: Data Inoculation (Levine group) stands out: a residual policy perturbs teleoperation during collection to harvest recovery-rich demonstrations. CuraEval and the action-interface study both deliver sobering analyses showing simple factors (episode length, action scaling) explain much of reported gains, while LOGSI gives a clean theory of logical guidance for stochastic interpolants. Catch It All shows zero-shot dexterous catching on a humanoid, and the VLA sample-efficiency study is a useful reference for picking a base model.
2026-10-29: An exceptional day for human-to-robot dexterity: TouchBridge, CIMI and the contact-wrench-space retargeting paper all transfer human demonstrations by aligning contact rather than kinematics, alongside the Tactus tactile glove and AcrossDEX. The 281-policy RJ45 study is a must-read on what actually drives real dexterous IL success. On the generative side, Coupled Guidance fixes diffusion-style guidance for flow matching, and movement-primitive action chunking targets smooth chunked execution.
2026-10-30: Geo-FSRL gives a principled answer to how noise should be injected when RL fine-tuning few-step flow models, and the DMD critic-scaling study offers sharp insight into few-step distillation. For dexterity, HandMimicX learns human-like skills from egocentric video via object-centric RL, TacMind benchmarks tactile interaction, and MotorSense adds EMG as a new human-hand signal. DMAT's direct clean-action modeling for one-step bimanual policies connects the day's theme of fast, few-step generative control.
2026-10-31: The standout theory piece is the degenerate-diffusion paper from Barber's group, which shows formally that flow matching is a deterministic-step diffusion model under a simple discrete-time variational objective. On the robot side, the tactile-foundation-model study (5,000+ real rollouts with Diffusion Policy) gives practical guidance for contact-rich IL, and the re-timing paper explains why sped-up demonstrations collapse: merged commands exceed the controller's per-step limit. Several VLA papers (Leap-VLA, JADE, PREM) explore tighter coupling between VLM and flow action experts, fast asynchronous inference, and memory.
2026-11-01: A strong day for this reader. Sun, Simchowitz and Song's 'Beyond Validation Loss' shows that closed-loop pass@k reveals a coverage-reliability tradeoff in generative-policy pretraining that predicts how well a checkpoint post-trains. ODE Policy proposes learning action dynamics with a neural ODE as an alternative to flow-matching policies and backs it with broad real-robot results, including dexterous hands. On the RL side, Value Forcing (Eysenbach group) uses flow matching for return distributions. On dexterity, GoalDex (pose-free, image-goal in-hand reorientation) and TF2-Steering (tactile residual steering of a flow action expert) both apply.
2026-11-02: The headline is AIRoA-0, a bimanual VLA trained on more than 16k hours of handheld-gripper demonstrations with no robot data; it reaches 78% on ten long-horizon real tasks, and the authors release the data and weights. For RL with generative policies, REPAIR distills RL specialists into a flow-matching VLA with critic-weighted flow matching and gets 100% real-robot success. The inertia-mismatch study from Agrawal's group gives a rigorous explanation of why heavy arms hurt behavior cloning. The day also has a strong tactile and contact-rich theme (PanoTac, ForceLDM, the visuotactile diffusion policy, DexArena) and two Pathak-group systems papers (Pixel, Pixel-UMI).
2026-11-03: RL with generative policies is the main theme. GSBR (Levine group) regularizes online RL toward the support of a diffusion/flow base policy rather than its full distribution and raises success from 33% to 95% over 19 tasks. CANDO combines noise-space steering with action-space residuals. For dexterity, GRASP (contact-rich retargeting, 92.8% on OakInk2), DexHOT (hand-object configuration transfer with real-hand results) and RoboTryOn (human-to-robot video try-on) all apply. World-action models also feature: DreamFree, FloMo and PrimeSim each show how video pretraining can feed control.
2026-11-04: RL for generalist policies stands out. 'RL Enables Scaling Generalist Robot Policy Improvement' finds that value-based RL can improve a foundation policy on many tasks at once and even helps on tasks it was not trained on. MAC-v2 (Levine) uses action chunking to make long-horizon model-based value expansion from pixels work. In generative modeling, Competitive Flow Matching trains a winner-take-all objective over K candidate velocities to widen the quality-coverage frontier, which could matter for multimodal policies. For dexterity, read the controlled tactile-cue study (marker flow wins over 720 real trials), the new full-stack dexterous-hand survey, and Open-HumanWAM's 50k-hour egocentric pretraining recipe.
2026-11-05: A strong day for generative-policy control. CS-Pi offers a clean draw-project-renoise sampler for enforcing unseen constraints on flow policies, and LARBRID gives noise-space RL fine-tuning of diffusion policies a linear-MDP footing. On the dexterity side, TactileLab brings scalable shear-aware tactile simulation with real in-hand transfer, while Latent RL Prior distills sim RL into a frozen flow decoder for data-efficient visual dexterity. GPWM and FewStepRL round out the theme of steering generative models through their noise or few-step structure.
2026-11-06: ODEAction directly challenges action chunking by evolving actions with a learned ODE, a must-skim for anyone thinking about chunk boundaries and streaming policies. BATCH (Shuran Song's group) aligns human and robot behaviors for video-action diffusion co-training, and MDF++ learns visuo-tactile world-action representations end-to-end for contact-rich insertion. Also notable: Apple's AMP1 argues generalist agents beat VLAs zero-shot, and Trajectory Forcing extends the diffusion-forcing line for AR video.
2026-11-07: Dexterity and tactile sensing dominate. SimDuoReal shows bimanual regrasping and handover emerging from a single object-centric RL reward with 76% real-world success, and GUARD steers diffusion policies with anomaly-informed Q-gradients for real in-hand screwdriver tasks. Two careful sensing studies (tactile vs wrist cameras; which taxels matter) and the vine-sampling paper on true multimodality in distilled diffusion policies are excellent 'understanding' reads. DPDP and the SMC view of MPPI add principled tools for diffusion RL and sampling-based control.
2026-11-08: DexForesight is the top pick, distilling an action-conditioned 3D hand-and-scene world model into dexterous policy latents with real-robot gains. For generative-model theory, EbbFlow improves MeanFlow training with a PINN-style temporal curriculum and a TTS paper neatly diagnoses why first-step CFG hurts few-step flow sampling. ObjectWorld's full-object 3D flow and the RoboEval RL-on-pi0.5 recipe are practical takeaways for world models and RL fine-tuning of VLAs.
2026-11-09: 'How Much of Your VLA Is kNN' is the must-read: retrieval of demo chunks reaches 91.7% on LIBERO, and fine-tuned VLAs mostly act as better retrieval keys. LingBot-Touch offers a cross-sensor tactile foundation model plugging into diffusion policies and VLAs, and VLA-MOPD consolidates flow-matching specialists via per-ODE-step on-policy distillation. Also worth a look: Grasping-the-Future's flow-matching hand-object forecasting from internet video, GAP's sim-to-real adaptation prior for piano playing, and a sharp analysis of how planners exploit quantization error in low-bit world models.
2026-11-10: ExRL is the standout: instead of RL-tuning high-dimensional action chunks, it learns only how long to execute each chunk, a cheap and usable adaptation knob for long-chunk policies. DexSeed expands human hand-object sequences into executable dexterous demos for VLA training, and 'Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock?' is a sharp diagnosis of temporal shortcuts in history-conditioned VLAs. The connecting theme is making chunked and memory-based policies robust and adaptable without massive new data.
2026-11-11: 'What Makes a VLA Reactive?' gives a rigorous empirical look at prediction/execution horizons and async chunk execution in pi0.5, with the finding that trajectory continuity matters more than raw latency. DexRemo pairs a high-force sensorized three-finger hand with ACT policies for contact-rich removal tasks. Also worth a look: CrowdMAPS widens IL datasets with multiple actions per state, and 'Prediction or Persistence?' shows V-JEPA future-prediction scores often hide a weak predictor.
2026-11-12: VOKE adds velocity and acceleration estimation to object pose trackers for vision-based in-hand manipulation, and InneR offers a principled Jacobian-based regularizer for robust behavior cloning. For world models and data, SALA and EgoX both tackle aligning human video with robot actions, while PixVid's finding that x-prediction plus a larger noise shift enables pixel-space video diffusion is a useful generative-modeling nugget.
2026-11-13: A strong tactile day: TouchTwin rebuilds glove-instrumented human demos in MuJoCo to close the 'force gap' of vision-only real-to-sim pipelines, and TMA uses tactile-driven motor adaptation for zero-shot sim-to-real forceful multi-finger doorknob opening. WATO trains joint world-action generators through differentiable trajectory optimization, and Kim/Jayaraman/Posa's study of visual representations for insertion is a careful understanding paper on contact-rich IL.
2026-11-14: 'Explicit Regularization for Flow Matching' examines why empirical flow matching memorizes near the data and how to regularize it, which is core generative-model theory. On policies, ResWAM supervises only future feature residuals for cheaper world-action models, and 'Refinement vs. Replanning' studies how chunked diffusion policies should spend inference compute. Ego2Sim2Humanoid and MARS round out the day with human-video-to-robot data and RL-refined VLA skills, and the MPPI exploration-as-feedback paper is a neat control insight.
2026-11-15: A strong day for generative-policy understanding. Behavioral Denoising (Manchester lab) proves closed-form diffusion policy weights solve a regularized behavioral control problem. Triangular-transport IL makes the source distribution of flow/interpolant policies a design choice, which allows one-step OT policies. On the dexterous side, DAPPT extends sim-to-real dexterous RL to deformable tool use and DexFormer 2.0 pushes cross-embodiment grasping. FlipTest is a sobering check on video world models: all 11 tested models score below random on counterfactual state tests.
2026-11-16: ALOHA Lightning (Finn lab) stands out: near-human-speed bimanual imitation from fast kinesthetic demos, with real-robot success above 80%. VLA-SSD is the pick for RL+generative policies: it distills a flow VLA into a stochastic one-step policy with tractable likelihood for GRPO. Human-hand data is a clear theme, with PriDex (human video to bimanual dexterous demos via RL), WinDEX and MetricHand (metric hand reconstruction), and the tactile encoders WiTac and TaF-Foundation. DreamFAR adds a fast robot-native world model for policy evaluation.
2026-11-17: RL and steering for flow policies dominate. Outcome-Balanced PPO with flow rectification targets flow VLAs, and Task Convergent Flow Matching searches source seeds with CMA-ES under progress funnels, a noise-space steering idea with guarantees. Advantage-Gated Adaptation gives a clean analysis of forward-process diffusion RL objectives. The RWM audit on ANYmal is a rigorous warning that one-step accuracy does not predict rollout or policy quality. Body Schema Policy and SR-VLA cover policy architecture and real-time execution.
2026-11-18: Most relevant for this reader: the dexterous VLA fine-tuning study on a LEAP hand finds the best SFT checkpoint is rarely the most steerable under DSRL, and recommends freezing the VLM and training the action expert. SHAPE and Ego2X show how to learn dexterity from egocentric human data, and 3DTouch adds base-frame visuotactile geometry to VLAs. World models as training environments are the second theme: WEVO's video-WM RL beats real-robot RL, and Doppel conditions on rendered bodies across eight embodiments. DUAC derives action-chunk uncertainty from the flow field.
2026-11-19: The standout is the radial-attention analysis of pi0.5, which shows the supposed action sink at chunk endpoints is just a RoPE artifact and that the executed prefix carries the signal, a careful 'why' study of action chunking in flow VLAs. TacHOI uses touch as a metric ruler for reconstructing hand-object interactions from egocentric video, and the JEPA-planner stall diagnosis (Unstick) explains why latent world-model planning gets stuck. RefreshGrad is a cheap data-sampling trick for diffusion policies worth a skim.
2026-11-20: A day of world-model and VLA deployment papers. GenPA argues image generators can be policies without future prediction, Ego4Gen generates 4D geometry and flow as a world-action interface, and PEA probes for invisible actuation shifts before running a VLA. Geo-Force offers a formal theory of virtual touch from depth geometry for those thinking about tactile substitutes.
2026-11-21: The top pick is the CFG error-activation paper, a rigorous Helmholtz-Hodge analysis of how guidance turns harmless score errors harmful, which bears directly on guided diffusion policies. ViewPACT shows proprioception acts as a shortcut and fixes viewpoint brittleness with privileged pose supervision, with real-robot gains. Most other papers are LLM/VLM RL or medical.
2026-11-22: A quiet day with one paper: MAWAM extends world action models to several robots by imagining their futures jointly. It fits the ongoing trend of world action models as policy backbones, though multi-robot collaboration sits next to the reader's dexterity focus.
2026-11-23: Agentic robotics dominates. Real2Worlds2Real has an agent build digital twins and cousins and run sim policy training end to end, and Robo-MOPD asks how to merge specialist tool-calling planners into one generalist. EmboEagle adds a learned gate so a flow-matching WAM calls its VLM supervisor only when needed. All three treat the low-level policy as a tool inside a bigger loop.
2026-11-24: The pick is the best-of-N steering paper: it shows that sampling more VLA candidates against an imperfect verifier leads to reward hacking, which is a real warning for verifier- or value-guided generative policies. SplatWAM offers an explicit 3D Gaussian world action model with a flow-matching policy head, and effect-driven skill abstractions tokenize action chunks by their outcomes for offline RL.
2026-11-25: A big day. Guidance as Variance Matching (Permenter, Jaakkola) explains CFG as restoring variance and predicts practical guidance scales in closed form. That is a must-read for the generative-theory side. On dexterity, DexEngine turns nine human HOI datasets into 578 h of physically executable arm-hand data, and DexLink chains retargeted pose templates with residual RL. Also worth a look: X-World (video prior + flow chunks + real-time chunking), iMFPO (MeanFlow policies with RL), and a 470k-rollout study of harness design for VLM-orchestrated VLAs.
